feature: Sound plays in step with the picture
summary: Pressing play used to bring the sound out about a fifth of a second behind the picture for the whole playthrough, so people talking in a recording looked dubbed. The sound now opens where the picture will be when it is first heard, and comes out within 20 ms of the picture on the 6 and 20 minute reference edits.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Any recording of someone talking, or the 20 minute reference edit.

try.do: Open a screen recording of someone talking and switch to Edit.
Press Space and watch their lips against their voice.
Press Space to stop, click the playhead somewhere in the middle, and press Space again.
Press L twice to play at double speed, then K, then J and L to compare at half speed.
Put on wireless headphones and play again.

evaluate: Do the lips and the voice look in step from the very first word after Space?
Is the short silence right after you press play (about a sixth of a second, as before) something you notice?
On wireless headphones, is it still in step?
rough: Measured, not heard: the walk reads which moment the sound engine says is reaching the speaker (its clock plus the output's reported latency) at the instant the picture reaches the screen. Before: 182 to 187 ms behind at the median, 168 to 201 ms worst. After: -3 to +5 ms at the median, -18 to +19 ms worst, over 120 one-second looks on the 6 and 20 minute edits.
Only measured on this Mac's current output, which reports 1 ms of latency. Wireless headphones report much more and the fix allows for whatever the output reports, but that case was not measured.
Only measured at normal speed. Half and double speed use the same arithmetic (unit tested) and their walks pass, but nothing yet measures their sync.

The task gave the limits as 45 ms late or 125 ms early. The broadcast standard it comes from (ITU-R BT.1359) has them the other way round: early sound is noticed sooner. The result is inside 45 ms either way, so it meets both.
